messages.author: 8605473662beac19
messages.subject: Re: before-and-after plot
parts:
Hi Hadley,
Thanks for the reply. And sorry if I did not explain myself clearly
before.
I would like to know how to build a before-and-after plot in ggplot2.
I have a recipe for building such a plot using other R packages, but
maybe it looks better in ggplot2. This kind of plot is used to
illustrate data analyzed with paired tests or any kind of data in
which each observation needs to be treated individually.

One example would be an experiment, in which 10 individual bats were
given a new type of food for one week. The weight (g) of each
individual bat was measured before and after the new food. The dataset
contains three columns: Individual, Before and After. The working
hypothesis was that the new food would promote weight gain in most
individuals.

You may see one example of such a plot here: http://db.tt/G9jFHVFc.
Thank you very much for your attention.

All the best,
Marco

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: before-and-after plot
parts:
Marco, you can build it setting the colour and linetype to an
aesthetic. Something like this

ggplot(dtf, aes(time, weight, colour = bat, linetype = bat) +
geom_line()

HTH
Luciano

showing. My data file may be downloaded here (http://db.tt/oD4pJ2sJ)
and the plot here (http://db.tt/ZOXtrIcs, made with other packages).

#Before-and-after plot

#Load the packages needed
require(lattice)
require(Matching)
require(MASS)
require(nlme)

given a new type of food for one week. The weight (g) of each

contains three columns: Individual, Before and After. The working

hypothesis is that the new food promotes weight gain in most

"After".

given the new food.

attach(df.new)

#Make the plot

interaction.plot(Time, Individual, Weight, ylab = "Body weight (g)",
xlab = "Time", main="Change in the body weight of bats after being
given a new food", col = rainbow(10))
dev.off()


#Detach df.new
detach(df.new)


#Make the plot in ggplot2

require(ggplot2)

ggplot(df.new, aes(Time, Weight, colour = Individual, linetype =
Individual)
+ geom_line()

======END======


Thanks!


Marco Mello

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: before-and-after plot
parts:
Dear Marco,

Here is what you want. You just needed to add the grouping when your x (or y) variable is a factor. Please check the rest of the code. Note that I don't use attach() and detach(). That's a disaster waiting to happen. Use the names of the data.frame instead or use something like with() or within().

newfood1 <- read.table("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/51420824/newfood1.txt", header = TRUE)

library(reshape)
df.new <- melt(newfood1, id.vars = "Individual", variable_name = "Time")
df.new$Weight <- df.new$value

with(df.new, interaction.plot(Time, Individual, Weight, ylab = "Body weight (g)", xlab = "Time", main="Change in the body weight of bats after being given a new food", col = rainbow(10)))
library(ggplot2)
df.new$Individual <- factor(df.new$Individual)
ggplot(df.new, aes(Time, Weight, colour = Individual, linetype = Individual, group = Individual)) + geom_line()

Best regards,

Thierry
